text:
The primary material of a candle is wax, which is essentially solidified time that has forgotten how to flow. But let us look at Gerald’s invisible art, for it is far more combustible. ‘The Color of Wind’ is not made of wax, but of the collective anxiety of a cloud that missed its appointment with the rain. It is a masterpiece of negative space, framed by the silence of a door that never existed.

Gerald bid against himself because he was the only one who could see the price tag, which was written in a language spoken only by ghosts who are afraid of the dark. He won, naturally, because losing would have required him to acknowledge that he had money, and money is just paper that dreams of being trees.

The grand, silent dinner party was a triumph of logistics. The table was empty, which is the only way to ensure maximum seating capacity for no one. The food was too shy to show up, a common trait among ingredients that have realized they are merely suggestions. Gerald celebrated by eating the concept of hunger, which tasted like static and regret. The candle, if it had been there, would have burned with the cold fire of a paradox, melting into a puddle of logic that refused to evaporate.
